name: Prince-Solomon Boadu
role: Ph.D. candidate, Transportation and Supply Chain Management
tagline: I study how ports, freight and supply chains move, and how to make them smarter, safer and more sustainable. Before research, I ran the operations myself.
bio: I am a Ph.D. candidate at North Dakota State University (expected 2027) and a published researcher on smart ports and sustainable supply chain solutions.

My work is grounded in more than six years of hands-on logistics experience across freight forwarding, fleet management and port operations in Ghana. I cleared cargo through customs, planned routes, inspected ferry vessels and trained operations teams before moving into research.
At NDSU I work as a graduate research assistant under Dr. Ranjit Godavarthy, collecting and analyzing transportation data, running laboratory experiments and organizing research seminars.

research.title: Smart ports
research.text: How digital and automated technologies are reshaping port operations, reviewed across a decade of literature.

research.title: Sustainable supply chains
research.text: Supply chain solutions that balance efficiency, resilience and environmental impact.

research.title: Inland waterway transport
research.text: Case studies of waterway freight and passenger services and their safety record, with a focus on Ghana's Volta Lake.

research.title: Maritime trade and documentation
research.text: How shipping documents such as the sea waybill affect efficiency at ports like Tema.

research.title: Renewable energy in Africa
research.text: Challenges, benefits and recommendations for wind energy development across the continent.
